waypoints.name: SR-20 Burgundy Col Pullout
waypoints.note: Long unmarked pullout on the east shoulder of SR-20 near milepost 165-166, about 4 miles east of Washington Pass; the climber's trail drops down the embankment on the east side.
waypoints.directions: From Washington Pass, drive SR-20 east about 3.75 miles, past the hairpin turn, to the next long pullout on the east shoulder near milepost 166, opposite Silver Star. The climbers' path is not signed — it drops off the east side of the embankment.

waypoints.name: Early Winters Creek Crossing
waypoints.note: Trail descends ~200 ft from the pullout to ford/log-cross Early Winters Creek; last reliable, easy water before the steep climb begins.
waypoints.directions: The boot path drops down the embankment through talus and into forest, passing a register box, and loses a little over 200 ft to a log crossing of Early Winters Creek. Fill up here: this is the last easy water before the climb, with only an unreliable trickle near the col above.

waypoints.name: The Bench
waypoints.note: Flat forested camping bench with multiple established tent sites and views toward the Liberty Bell group; common first-night camp for a two-day trip.
waypoints.directions: From the creek the trail turns east and climbs steeply and continuously, gaining roughly 2,400 ft in a mile and a half of forest to the flat bench. This is about the halfway point of the approach by both distance and gain, which is why parties splitting the trip camp here.

waypoints.name: Burgundy Col
waypoints.note: 7,770-ft notch gained via 1,000+ ft of loose ball-bearing scree; from here descend/traverse loose rock or steep snow around the north face to reach the route.
waypoints.directions: Above the bench the ground opens into loose scree gullies, finishing with a cairned stretch of unstable scree over slab to the notch. This is the crux of the approach in both directions — the ball-bearing scree is the main hazard on the route, and the col's east side can hold snow or ice into summer.

waypoints.name: Splitter flake start
waypoints.note: About 5-10 minutes below the col via loose rock/snow scramble to a clean splitter flake; P1 climbs the flake system to a roof pull and lieback on the left.
waypoints.directions: Do not start climbing at the col. Scramble down and around the base of Burgundy's north face on loose rock, or on steep snow that can want an axe into midsummer, for five to ten minutes until you are directly under a clean splitter flake. The start sits about 15 ft climber's-left of Ultramega OK's twin cracks, so it is further along the base than both the North Face's start and Ultramega OK's.

waypoints.name: Burgundy Spire Summit
waypoints.note: Eight varied, loose and lichen-covered pitches (crux 5.10c) top out at the summit; standard descent is the North Face's 5-rappel line (double ropes) back toward the col.
waypoints.directions: Eight pitches: a flake system to a roof pull and lieback, a right-trending finger crack, then the lichened, steep 5.10c finger crack that is the crux. Fourth-class ground trends left to a chimney, then a poor-rock corner and steep, thinly-protected bulges at 5.10 with the belay beyond the arete. The last pitch either rambles up to 5.7 past an old bolt to the skyline and the true summit, or traverses Burgundy Ledge into the standard North Face route — the descent is the North Face rappel line either way.

waypoints.name: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road
Eldorado Creek / Cascade River Road TH
waypoints.note: Large pullout at mile 20 of Cascade River Road; cross the Cascade River on a log/flagged crossing to the climbers' trail.
waypoints.directions: From Marblemount, follow Cascade River Road south about 20 miles to the parking area near mile 20 — paved for the first 10 miles, gravel and washboard after that. Any overnight needs a free North Cascades backcountry permit, reserved in advance on Recreation.gov or drawn from the walk-up allocation in person at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center.

waypoints.name: Eldorado (East Ridge) camp
waypoints.note: High camp on the Inspiration Glacier flat used as base for Eldorado's satellite peaks.
waypoints.directions: Backtrack a short distance along the road from the lot to find a safe crossing of the Cascade River — historically a large log or a braided ford, and it shifts from year to year. On the far side a steep, unmaintained climbers' path gains 3,000-3,500 ft through old-growth forest to a boulder field, crosses Eldorado Creek and opens into the meadows of the Eldorado Creek basin, then continues onto glacier to the camp on the Inspiration flat. Figure 5-6 hours from the car, with roped travel and crevasse-rescue gear needed above the meadows.

waypoints.name: Klawatti col
waypoints.note: Break in the ridge above the McAllister Glacier; rappel ~75 ft to the Klawatti Glacier.
waypoints.directions: Rope up and traverse the Inspiration Glacier northeast at roughly 7,800 ft, continuing well past Eldorado's own summit and the Tepeh Towers to the col on Klawatti's flank. Pass through the col and follow Klawatti's north ridge along the upper reaches of the McAllister Glacier to the break in the ridge at about 7,900 ft.

waypoints.name: Klawatti Glacier crevasses
waypoints.note: Traverse high and left across the crevassed Klawatti Glacier toward Austera.
waypoints.directions: Work through the moat below the break — usually straightforward by August, more of a problem early season or in a heavy snow year — then rappel about 75 ft onto the Klawatti Glacier. Leave a retrievable cordelette rather than fixed gear, since the exit reverses this pitch on lead at about 5.5. Rope up again and traverse the glacier high and climber's left toward Austera; the Klawatti has receded a great deal, so expect the crossing to be more broken than older descriptions suggest, and the peak itself does not resolve until you are close.

waypoints.name: Austera Peak
waypoints.note: Final 30 ft of low 5th-class climbing on the northeast face.
waypoints.directions: Leave the glacier where the traverse runs out below the peak and scramble a few hundred feet of 4th class, then trend and traverse left along a broken ridge to the sub-summit. A final short pitch of well-protected low 5th class swings right onto the northeast face to the true summit; the rock on the summit tower is loose enough to be worth belaying.

removed.wp: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road

waypoints.name: Barclay Lake Trailhead (end of FS Road 6024)
waypoints.directions: In Baring, turn north off US 2 onto 635th Place NE, across from the store. Cross the railroad tracks, keep left at the junction just beyond, and follow the road as it becomes FS Road 6024, about 4.3 miles in all, to the Barclay Lake Trailhead at the road end, about 2,280 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

waypoints.name: Baring Mountain north (main) summit
waypoints.directions: Skip Trail 1055: walk the old logging road behind the toilet 0.3 mile to the first creek, where a cairn on the right marks a steep climbers' path that crosses the creek twice and climbs to the west ridge crest near 4,000 ft. Follow the crest east a mile, drop below the cliff bands on the south side, cross a wooded gully to the talus basin at 4,900 ft, climb the couloir to the 5,550 ft notch, then go north on easy Class 3 to the top.

waypoints.name: FS Road 3160 End Trailhead
waypoints.note: End of the rough, single-lane FS Road 3160 (high-clearance/4x4 recommended); unmaintained boot path to Church Lake starts here.
waypoints.directions: Drive Canyon Creek Road (FS-31) north off SR-542 just east of Glacier, then FS-3160 to its end at about 4,800 ft. The upper road is single-lane and rough, high clearance is the usual advice, and the parking is no more than a wide spot at the end.

waypoints.name: Boot Path Junction / Old Roadbed
waypoints.note: Unmarked user-built path leaves the old roadbed and climbs through brush toward the lake basin.
waypoints.directions: Continue on the old roadbed past the parking area for a couple of hundred yards. The user-built path toward the lake basin leaves it unmarked, though motorbike use has worn the line in well enough to follow.

waypoints.name: Church Lake
waypoints.note: Emerald subalpine lake in a basin below Bearpaw; established rough camp spots on the shore, often overgrown approach.
waypoints.directions: The path climbs steeply through forest — the steepest sustained grade of the day, about 400 ft — then rolls over a rise into the cirque holding the lake, 0.6 to 0.7 mile from the car.

waypoints.name: Left Rim of Church Lake Basin
waypoints.note: Keep left around the lake and start climbing the rim of the basin toward Point 6066 rather than following the lakeshore fully around.
waypoints.directions: Skirt the lake along its east/left shore rather than following the shoreline the whole way around, then start up the rim of the basin on the left (east) toward Point 6066. Fill water at the lake; there is none above it.

waypoints.name: Steep Heather/Meadow Ridge Below Point 6066
waypoints.note: Steep, loose tread through heather and meadow gains the ridge crest; described by hikers as steep but 'nothing scary' in dry conditions, slick when wet.
waypoints.directions: Above the lake the tread fades into intermittent boot path and cairns through meadow and heather benches, and the rim steepens on loose footing. Straightforward when dry, genuinely slick when wet, and snow lingers on the shaded slopes here into midsummer.

waypoints.name: Point 6066 Knoll
waypoints.note: Knoll with 270-degree views from Mount Baker eastward into Canada; the narrow summit ridge to Bearpaw's true top begins here.
waypoints.directions: Keep working up the rim to the broad high point on the ridge dividing Church Lake's basin from Bearpaw's summit block. This stretch accounts for most of the day's remaining gain.

waypoints.name: Exposed Summit Ridge
waypoints.note: Narrow, sometimes exposed ridgeline with loose footing for the final approach; use caution, easy to slip off either side.
waypoints.directions: From the knoll drop slightly and traverse north across a rocky, heathery bowl toward the base of the summit block, picking up the narrow connecting ridge. Footing is loose and the crest is exposed on both sides in places.

waypoints.name: Bearpaw Mountain
waypoints.note: True summit; final ~100m from the ridge is a short Class 2-3 scramble over blocky rock.
waypoints.directions: The last stretch is a short Class 2-3 scramble, roughly 100 m, on generally solid blocky rock with mild exposure. Reverse the same ground to descend, or drop the scree-and-dirt chute that cuts straight from the ridge down to the lakeshore — quicker, but loose enough that it is no place to be below another party.

waypoints.name: Blue Lake Trailhead
waypoints.note: Blue Lake Trail #314 trailhead on SR-20; shared approach for Liberty Bell and South Early Winters Spire (NW Forest Pass required).
waypoints.directions: Drive SR-20 (the North Cascades Highway) to the Blue Lake Trailhead on the south side of the highway just west of Washington Pass. The highway over the pass closes in winter. A Northwest Forest Pass or day fee is required to park.

waypoints.name: South Early Winters Spire
waypoints.note: True summit of South Early Winters Spire, between Liberty Bell and Blue Lake Peak.
waypoints.directions: Hike the Blue Lake Trail about 1.25 miles to the clearing where the main trail bends right toward the lake, and take the climbers' path up into the basin to the Y-shaped larch at the base of the Southwest Rib, left of the Southwest Couloir. Climb the first three pitches of the rib, go left at the ledge where the two stacked roofs come into view, pull through them, and finish up the remaining rib pitches to the summit.

waypoints.name: Alpental Ski Area parking lot / Snow Lake Trailhead
waypoints.note: Same trailhead used for all Chair Peak-area routes; from here the traverse starts up the Snow Lake Trail to the Source Lake fork and the basin below Chair Peak.
waypoints.directions: From I-90 take Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West) and turn left (north), passing under the freeway. Take the second right onto Alpental Road and drive about 1.3 miles to its end at the Alpental Ski Area parking lot, at about 3,100 ft, where the Snow Lake Trail #1013 starts. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free self-issue wilderness permit is required.

waypoints.name: Chair Peak
waypoints.directions: Take the Snow Lake Trail to the Source Lake fork, then climbers' paths and a gully to roughly 4,800 ft and the basin below Chair Peak. Gain Chair's north ridge and follow it to the summit.

waypoints.name: Bryant Peak
waypoints.directions: Follow the crest southeast from Chair's summit, down to Bryant Col and on along the ridge to Bryant Peak, on 4th-class to low-5th-class rock that is loose in places.

waypoints.name: Alpental parking lot / Snow Lake TH #1013
waypoints.directions: Take I-90 to Exit 52 at Snoqualmie Pass and follow Alpental Road to its end, parking in the upper Alpental lot at about 3,100 feet. The Snow Lake Trail #1013 starts here; a cat track leaves the end of the lot and runs up the valley just left of the stream. Plan an alpine start, since this route is normally done car-to-car in one long day.

waypoints.name: Chair Peak Lake (basin below the east face)
Snow Lake Trailhead (Alpental)
waypoints.directions: From I-90 take Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West) and turn left (north), passing under the freeway. Take the second right onto Alpental Road and drive about 1.3 miles to its end at the Alpental Ski Area parking lot, at about 3,100 ft, where the Snow Lake Trail #1013 starts. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free self-issue wilderness permit is required.

waypoints.name: Northwest Ridge base
waypoints.directions: Follow the Snow Lake Trail to the Source Lake fork, then the climbers' path and snow up the basin toward Chair Peak's east face; about two hours in you reach Thumbtack Rock, the small pinnacle that marks the turn. Turn right there and climb a grassy gully over the ridge onto the northwest side, then head for a saddle with trees on it; the route starts up the gully just left of that saddle.

waypoints.name: Chair Peak summit
waypoints.directions: Climb the gully left of the treed saddle to the crest and belay from trees on its south side. Scramble down and left to the chockstone-capped chimney, work around and over the chockstone onto the ridge, then follow the easier, run-out crest past a false summit to the true summit, avoiding the loose, harder lines off the crest.

waypoints.name: SR-20 Wine Spires pullout (milepost 166)
waypoints.note: Unmarked highway pullout ~2-4 miles east of the Washington Pass hairpin turn; climbers descend to Early Winters Creek then switchback up to Burgundy Col.
waypoints.directions: Drive SR-20 to the unsigned pullout near milepost 166, roughly four miles east of Washington Pass, at about 4,300 ft. There is no sign and no developed trailhead here, only a broad shoulder pullout, so watch your odometer. Check WSDOT before travelling: the highway is gated shut through the winter and reopens somewhere between mid-April and late June depending on snowpack and slide repair.

waypoints.name: Burgundy Creek bench camp — west side
Burgundy Col
waypoints.directions: From the pullout, drop off the highway on a steep, faint boot path and descend the talus to Early Winters Creek, crossing on logs. Climb the far side on the climber's path, switchbacking up talus benches and loose cairned gullies through timber and boulders; where the boot track braids, stay climber's-left, keeping north of the drainage coming down from the basin below the spires, and aim for the obvious notch of the col. It is about 3,500 ft of gain and 3-4 hours with an overnight pack, and snow can linger in the gully below the col into July, so carry an axe early in the season.

waypoints.name: Chianti Spire / East Face (Rebel Yell) area
waypoints.directions: Drop off the col down a short snow and rock step and traverse south beneath the east face of Burgundy Spire, crossing a small snowy rib onto the upper Silver Star Glacier, then around to the obvious east side of Chianti Spire at about 7,900 ft. Reckon on under an hour from the col, or from the larch bench camp lower down. Carry an ice axe through midsummer, as the rib and the glacier margin are often firm or icy first thing in the morning.

waypoints.name: Chianti Spire Summit
waypoints.directions: Seven pitches of gear-protected crack climbing up the east face, four to six hours for most parties. Start up flakes into the obvious wide dihedral, taking either the easier right-hand start or the thinner left-hand finger crack, which rejoins by the top of pitch 1, then the offwidth and the lower-angle dihedral above, then the balancy blind step left across the arete past a fixed bolt on pitch 4. Pitch 5 is the technical crux, a sustained thin-hands crack widening through cupped hands to fists and capped by a strenuous offwidth move, and pitch 6 follows the same system to a rising ramp trending left to the exposed summit block, gained by short final moves past a single bolt.

waypoints.name: Klipchuck Campground, with Early Winters nearby
Cutthroat Peak Climbers Trail Pullout (Hwy 20, ~1.5 mi W of Washington Pass)
waypoints.note: Same shared approach pullout/trail as the standard South Buttress route.
waypoints.directions: Drive SR-20 to the long pullout on the north side of the highway about 1.5 miles west of Washington Pass, at roughly 4,950 ft. It is the same pullout the standard South Buttress uses, and the cairned climbers' track leaves from its east end, dropping through timber toward State Creek. Reckon on a July-to-September season for this route.

waypoints.name: Toe of the lower ridge (start of the Complete South Buttress)
waypoints.directions: From the pullout, follow the cairned climbers' track down through timber, across State Creek (the last reliable water), and up into the meadows and boulder field below the peak to about 6,500 ft. Where the standard South Buttress track bears right toward its entry gully, leave the path and contour southeast on talus and heather benches, off-trail, to the very bottom of the ridge, where easy ledgy slabs mark its toe.

waypoints.name: Cutthroat Peak Summit
waypoints.directions: From the easy, ledgy slabs at the toe of the lower ridge, follow the crest on 3rd, 4th and easy 5th class ground, making two half-rope rappels from old tat into notches. Where the ridge merges with the standard South Buttress, continue up its crest past a chimney with a big chockstone and a wide stembox, downclimb into the notch, climb a corner and a hand-to-offwidth crack, and cross the big slab to the summit.

removed.wp: Klipchuck Campground, with Early Winters nearby

waypoints.name: Klipchuck Campground, with Early Winters nearby
Cutthroat Peak Climbers Trail Pullout (Hwy 20, ~1.5 mi W of Washington Pass, north side)
waypoints.note: Same starting pullout as South Buttress approach; route then diverges east across the south rib into the basin below the East Face rather than continuing to the south basin
waypoints.directions: Drive the North Cascades Highway (SR-20) to the long pullout on the north side of the road about 1.5 miles west of Washington Pass, roughly half a mile west of the Blue Lake Trailhead. The climbers' track leaves the east end of the pullout. SR-20 over Washington Pass is gated in winter, so this route's season begins when the highway reopens in spring.

waypoints.name: Cutthroat Peak
waypoints.directions: Take the cairned climbers' track from the east end of the pullout down through timber, cross State Creek, and climb toward the basin below the south side of the peak. Cross the rib running south from the South Buttress into the basin east of the peak, climb the big couloir splitting the East Face through its ice steps to the ridgeline, then climb short pitches of about 5.4 rock to the true summit.

removed.wp: Klipchuck Campground, with Early Winters nearby

waypoints.name: Klipchuck Campground, with Early Winters nearby
Cutthroat Peak Climbers Trail Pullout (Hwy 20, ~1.5 mi W of Washington Pass, north side)
waypoints.note: Shared with the Cauthorn-Wilson Couloir and the other east-side routes, which reach the basin east of the peak over the rib south of the South Buttress.
waypoints.directions: Drive the North Cascades Highway (SR-20) to the long pullout on the north side of the road about 1.5 miles west of Washington Pass, roughly half a mile west of the Blue Lake Trailhead. The climbers' track leaves the east end of the pullout. SR-20 over Washington Pass is closed in winter, typically from late fall until spring.

waypoints.name: Cutthroat Peak
waypoints.directions: Take the cairned climbers' track from the east end of the pullout down through timber, cross State Creek, and climb toward the basin below the south side of the peak. Cross the rib running south from the South Buttress into the basin east of the peak, avoiding the loose scree chimneys directly below the wall. Six pitches up the East Face, with two 5.10 pitches near the center, end on a false summit.

removed.wp: Klipchuck Campground, with Early Winters nearby

waypoints.name: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road
Eldorado Creek Trailhead (Cascade River Road)
waypoints.note: Same start as the standard Southwest Buttress; cross the Cascade River on a log downstream of the parking area.
waypoints.directions: From SR 20 at Marblemount, cross the Skagit River and follow the Cascade River Road about 20 miles, gravel for the second half, to the small Eldorado trailhead lot on the right near milepost 20, about 2,100 ft. Overnight stays need a North Cascades backcountry permit from the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center.

waypoints.name: Eldorado/Inspiration Glacier high camp
waypoints.note: Base camp on the Inspiration Glacier shelf shared with the standard Southwest Buttress route.
waypoints.directions: From the lot, walk about 90 feet back down the road and look for the log or clump of trees spanning the river; cross there, then head roughly 100 feet away from the water to pick up the climbers' path and turn upstream on it. The path climbs steeply through forest and talus into Eldorado Basin and on up to the Inspiration Glacier shelf, about 5,500 ft of gain to camps near 7,400-7,600 ft.

waypoints.name: Inspiration–McAllister Glacier col
waypoints.note: Crossing point from Inspiration Glacier onto the McAllister Glacier, shared with the standard buttress approach.
waypoints.directions: Rope up at camp and cross the Inspiration Glacier northeast to the low point on the divide. The ground is otherwise gentle; crevasses are the only real difficulty.

waypoints.name: Marble Creek–McAllister pass
waypoints.note: Shared approach point; the Direct variant leaves the standard line at the top of the approach gully, going straight up where the standard route traverses right.
waypoints.directions: Drop off the col onto the McAllister Glacier and work down and across it, keeping to its skier's right where the ice steepens and breaks up, then traverse toward the pass.

waypoints.name: Direct Southwest Buttress topout
waypoints.note: Harder direct start (5.10a) rejoins the standard buttress line before the final corner to the summit ridge.
waypoints.directions: About 700 vertical feet below the pass, start up the prominent gully running to the base of the buttress; it usually holds snow year-round. Rope up before its top, because the moat guarding the base of the rock can open into a deep, exposed gap. From the gully exit do not traverse right onto the standard 1985 line: carry straight on up two direct pitches of 4th and low-5th scrambling to three vertical cracks, take the rightmost at about 5.8 into the strenuous 5.10 crux and mantel onto a large bench, then follow awkward 5.8+ ground toward the large white slabby rock where the original route comes back in.

waypoints.name: Dorado Needle summit
waypoints.note: True summit shared with the standard Southwest Buttress finish.
waypoints.directions: From the junction with the 1985 line, blocky mid-5th rock and a final corner lead onto the summit ridge, then a short scramble along it gains the true summit.

removed.wp: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road

waypoints.name: SR-20 Wine Spires pullout / Burgundy Col climbers' trail
waypoints.note: Unmarked roadside pullout on North Cascades Hwy near MP166, ~0.7mi from the Cutthroat Lake Rd junction. Trail drops to and crosses Early Winters Creek, then climbs steeply to the ~6,500ft bench camp below the spires — the shared base for all Wine Spires routes including this one.
waypoints.directions: Drive the North Cascades Highway (SR 20) to the unmarked pullout on the south side of the highway near milepost 166, about 0.7 mile west of the Cutthroat Lake Road turnoff (east of Washington Pass and its hairpin). No pass is needed to park at this roadside pullout.

waypoints.name: Burgundy Creek bench camp — west side
Pernod Spire Summit
waypoints.directions: Take the climbers' boot path down to Early Winters Creek at about 4,080 ft and cross on logs, then climb steeply through forest between two feeder gullies to the bench camp near 6,500 ft. From the bench leave the Burgundy Col trail and go up and right (east) past two minor buttresses into the broad talus gully under the tallest wall, then climb the eight pitches of the West Face to the summit block.

waypoints.name: Blue Lake Trailhead
waypoints.note: Blue Lake Trail #314 trailhead on SR-20; shared approach for Liberty Bell and South Early Winters Spire (NW Forest Pass required).
waypoints.directions: Drive the North Cascades Highway (SR 20) to the signed Blue Lake Trailhead on the south side of the highway, about 1 mile west of Washington Pass, at roughly 5,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

waypoints.name: South Early Winters Spire
waypoints.note: True summit of South Early Winters Spire, between Liberty Bell and Blue Lake Peak.
waypoints.directions: Hike the Blue Lake Trail about 1.25 miles to the signed clearing northwest of Liberty Bell, then take the climbers' path up talus and heather into the basin below the spire's west side, aiming for the Y-shaped larch at the base of the Southwest Rib. Climb two or three pitches of the rib, traverse left to the dark chimney about 100 ft left of the Boving Roof, climb it, and finish on easier cracks up the rib to the summit.

waypoints.name: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road
Eldorado Creek trailhead (Cascade River Road mile 20)
waypoints.directions: Drive Cascade River Road from Marblemount about 20 miles to the Eldorado Creek trailhead, near 2,100 ft. The first ten miles are paved and the remainder is rough gravel, so high clearance is recommended. Park in the roadside lot at mile 20; from there the walking starts by crossing the North Fork Cascade River on logs and picking up the steep climbers' path beside Eldorado Creek.

waypoints.name: Col between Pt. 8386 and Dorado Needle (East Ridge start)
waypoints.directions: Cross the river on logs and climb the steep climbers' path beside Eldorado Creek, then the boulder fields and the Eldorado Glacier to the East Ridge of Eldorado Peak and the high camps near 7,400 ft, roughly 4 miles and 6,000 ft of gain. From camp, rope up and traverse the Inspiration Glacier onto the McAllister Glacier to the col between Point 8386 and Dorado Needle, about 7,600 ft.

waypoints.name: Dorado Needle summit
waypoints.directions: Climb straight off the col on loose, thin first-pitch rock (a slung horn sits about 100 ft up), then several ropelengths along the ridge. Drop into a notch, traverse the glacier to a ledge with pale quartzite bands (watch the moat) and regain the ridge to the sub-summit tower. Two short rappels reach the notch below the summit, then two 5.7 crack pitches lead to the top.

removed.wp: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road

waypoints.name: FR6517 Roadside Parking
waypoints.note: Pull-off on FR6517, reached via FR6510 and FR6514 off Beckler River Road (FR65) — about 10.8 mi of gravel forest road; parking sits roughly 0.5 mi east of the summit.
waypoints.directions: From Skykomish take the Beckler River Road (FR 65) north, then follow the FR 6510 / FR 6514 / FR 6517 spur network — about 10.8 miles of gravel and dirt past the pavement — to the road end. The spurs can be rough or snow-blocked into early summer. There is no maintained trail beyond the pull-off and no water anywhere above the car, so carry all of it from here.

waypoints.name: Brush Exit / Open Forest
waypoints.note: Route leaves the roadside brush and enters open forest within a few hundred feet of the parking pull-off — head west, straight up the hillside.
waypoints.directions: Leave the road and head west-southwest, straight up the hillside. There is no trail and no cairns, so the line is picked by eye. A short push through roadside brush puts you into open timber within the first few hundred feet.

waypoints.name: Talus Below NE Cliffs
waypoints.note: A few hundred yards past the forest edge, trees give way to loose talus beneath Eagle Rock's northeast cliff band — watch for rockfall from above and unstable blocks underfoot.
waypoints.directions: Keep climbing west through the timber; after a few hundred yards the trees thin and the ground turns to open talus. It is steep — nearly all of the route's roughly 1,400 ft of gain is packed into the 0.8 mile from the car, so it feels considerably bigger than the mileage suggests.

waypoints.name: Start of Counterclockwise Traverse
waypoints.note: Begin the ascending, counterclockwise traverse around the peak toward its north side; stay on talus, avoiding the cliff bands directly above.
waypoints.directions: Do not push straight up into the cliffs from the base of the talus: parties who take the direct line up the northeast side get cliffed out. Start a rising traverse to climber's left instead, holding the arc across loose talus and scree below the rock rather than gaining height too fast.

waypoints.name: North Side Scramble Start (~5000')
waypoints.note: On reaching the north side at about 5000', the final pitch splits: an easier Class 2 line on the right or a steeper Class 2/3 line straight up the center.
waypoints.directions: Hold the counterclockwise arc around onto the peak's north side, gaining a couple of hundred feet across talus to the broad bench. Fix the line in your head as you go — this traverse is what you reverse, and in poor visibility it is easy to drift back toward the cliff bands on the way down.

waypoints.name: Eagle Rock Summit
waypoints.note: True summit after roughly 600' of Class 2/3 scrambling from the north-side base; round trip from the car is typically under 3 hours.
waypoints.directions: From the bench, angle southwest a few hundred yards to the foot of the summit slope, then take about 600 vertical feet of open slope and talus to the top. A far-left finish adds around 50 ft of slightly exposed Class 3; some parties carry a short length of rope to rig a handline there, though neither of the standard lines needs one.

waypoints.name: SR-20 Wine Spires pullout (milepost 166)
waypoints.note: Approach via Silver Star Creek drainage or the Burgundy Col climbers trail.
waypoints.directions: Drive the North Cascades Highway (SR 20) east past Washington Pass and its hairpin to the pullout on the south side of the highway near milepost 166, about 0.7 mile west of the Cutthroat Lake Road turnoff. No pass is needed to park at this roadside pullout.

waypoints.name: Chablis Spire - Summit
waypoints.note: East Face; the tiny summit is reached by a short unprotected lead, one climber at a time; distinctive bunny-ears profile.
waypoints.directions: Take the boot path down across Early Winters Creek and up the timbered rib north of Burgundy Creek to the bench camp near 6,500 ft, then on to Burgundy Col at about 7,720 ft. Drop 200 to 300 ft down the col's east side (steep snow, loose rock or moats by season) and traverse south beneath the east faces to Chablis, the southernmost spire, then climb the four pitches of the East Face to the summit.

waypoints.name: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road
Eldorado Creek / Cascade River Road TH
waypoints.directions: In Marblemount, where SR 20 turns, go straight onto Cascade River Road and cross the Skagit River bridge. Follow the road about 20 miles to the small Eldorado parking area on the right at about 2,100 ft, with a pit toilet. The first 10 miles are paved and the rest is rough gravel. The road usually opens in late May or June. Overnight stays need a park backcountry permit, picked up in person at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center.

waypoints.name: Eldorado (East Ridge) camp
waypoints.directions: Walk about 90 ft back down the road and cross the Cascade River on the log, then go about 100 ft straight away from the river to the climbers' path. It climbs steeply through timber to a boulder field; follow cairns up it, staying climber's right of Eldorado Creek, into Eldorado Creek Basin. Cross the ridge at about 6,100 ft into Roush Basin, take talus and slabs onto the Eldorado Glacier, rope up, and climb to the East Ridge camp near 7,500 to 7,600 ft.

waypoints.name: Base of North Ridge
waypoints.note: The notch between the North Ridge and the first rock spire north of it, shared with the Northwest Ice Couloir rappel.
waypoints.directions: Roped, cross the Inspiration Glacier past the east end of the East Ridge, then traverse the glacier on the mountain's north side at about 8,100 ft to the obvious notch between the North Ridge and the first rock spire north of it. Do not rappel the far side; that is the way into the Northwest Ice Couloir.

waypoints.name: Eldorado Peak
waypoints.note: Exposed granite ridge crest, moves up to 5.7, leading to the summit.
waypoints.directions: Climb steep snow out of the notch onto the rock crest, then follow the ridge on its east side, where the rock is solid with good friction and incut holds (moves to 5.7). Near the top, either finish directly up steeper ice and rock or join the East Ridge knife-edge to the summit.

removed.wp: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road

waypoints.name: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road
Eldorado Creek Trailhead
waypoints.directions: In Marblemount, where SR 20 turns, go straight onto Cascade River Road and cross the Skagit River bridge. Follow the road about 20 miles to the small Eldorado parking area on the right at about 2,100 ft, with a pit toilet. The first 10 miles are paved and the rest is rough gravel. The road usually opens in late May or June. Overnight stays need a park backcountry permit, picked up in person at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center.

waypoints.name: Eldorado Peak Summit
waypoints.directions: Cross the Cascade River on the log and climb the climbers' path and boulder field into Eldorado Creek Basin, then go over the ridge into Roush Basin and up the Eldorado Glacier. Near 7,500 ft, leave the East Ridge track to climber's right onto the Northeast Face. Traverse below the rock band near 8,200 ft to a point northeast of the summit, climb the face (up to 60 degrees) to the start of the knife-edge, and follow the crest to the summit.

removed.wp: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road

waypoints.name: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road
Eldorado Creek Trailhead (Cascade River Road)
waypoints.note: Same Cascade River Road trailhead as the standard route; the route follows the standard climbers' trail from the North Fork Cascade River up Eldorado Creek and into the Roush Creek basin before crossing the Inspiration and McAllister glaciers to Dorado Needle Col and the West Face.
waypoints.directions: From SR-20 at Marblemount, cross the Skagit River onto Cascade River Road and drive about 20 miles (pavement gives way to gravel around mile 10) to the parking area at about 2,100 ft near Eldorado Creek. Overnight stays in North Cascades National Park need a backcountry permit. The road is often not open this far until late June.

waypoints.name: Eldorado Peak
waypoints.directions: Cross the Cascade River on logs a short way downstream of the parking and follow the steep climbers' trail up beside Eldorado Creek into the Roush Creek basin and onto the Eldorado Glacier. From the glacier, descend west into the Marble Creek cirque to the toe of the arete near 6,000 ft, then climb the arete, about 2,800 ft of loose 4th class to 5.8 on and near the crest, to the summit.

removed.wp: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road

waypoints.name: Squire Creek Park & Campground, Snohomish County
Squire Creek Road Trailhead
waypoints.note: Access from Darrington via Squire Creek Road to blocked parking; road washed out ~2 mi in.
waypoints.directions: From Seattle, take I-5 north to the Arlington exit and follow SR 530 east through Oso to Darrington. Turn south on Madison Avenue to the T, go right on Darrington Street, and follow it as it becomes Squire Creek Road at the west end of town. Drive to the end of the road, about 1,100 feet, where a washout roughly two miles in gates it and blocks the parking area. Park at the gate; the old roadbed beyond it is walking only.

waypoints.name: Waterfall Basin (base of walls)
waypoints.note: About 2 hr to the basin via old roadbed, streambed, and a Squire Creek ford, below Three Fingers' east face. The foot of Roan Wall is higher still, and Salish Peak's base farther on, up the left side of Roan Wall: about 6 hr from the car in all.
waypoints.directions: Walk the old roadbed past a flagged landslide crossing and the original road end to a wide, dry streambed of white boulders. Descend the bed about 200 ft, trend left into the alders to find the informal path, and follow it to the ford of Squire Creek, then on as the trail fades until the basin opens. Scramble the thin boulder-filled watercourse that comes down from the wall to the base beside Martha's Place, the huge overhung boulder.

waypoints.name: Salish Peak summit
waypoints.note: Top of Flight of the Falcon. Most parties rappel from Falcon's Perch atop pitch 7 instead of continuing here.
waypoints.directions: From the basin, climb the bolted 5.8 approach slab and the dirty low-fifth crack to the foot of Roan Wall, scramble up its left side to the saddle where Salish Peak comes into view, and cross the high basin to the toe of the south face, about 6 hours from the car in all. Climb the route's nine pitches to the summit.

removed.wp: Squire Creek Park & Campground, Snohomish County

waypoints.name: Blue Lake Trailhead
waypoints.note: Blue Lake Trail #314 trailhead on SR-20; shared approach for Liberty Bell and South Early Winters Spire (NW Forest Pass required).
waypoints.directions: The Blue Lake trailhead is on the south side of SR-20 near milepost 162, about a mile west of Washington Pass, at about 5,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

waypoints.name: South Early Winters Spire
waypoints.note: True summit of South Early Winters Spire, between Liberty Bell and Blue Lake Peak.
waypoints.directions: Follow the Blue Lake Trail to the clearing on the northwest side of the spires, then take the climbers' path up talus into the basin below the west face. Free Mojo starts on a plain crack about 40 ft down and right of the big chockstone-filled chimney between the two formations, and six pitches lead to the summit.

waypoints.name: Barclay Lake Trailhead (FR-6024)
waypoints.directions: From Monroe, drive east on US-2 to Baring and, near milepost 41-42 across from the convenience store, turn left (north) onto 635th Place NE. Cross the railroad tracks and continue about 0.3 mile to a junction, keep left on 635th Place NE for another 0.1 mile, and the road becomes Forest Road 6024 (Barclay Creek Road). Follow roughly 3.9 to 4.3 miles of gravel to the Barclay Lake Trailhead, watching for potholes and rough patches — AWD or 4x4 is recommended after wet weather. There is a vault toilet and parking for about 20 vehicles, and a Northwest Forest Pass is required.

waypoints.name: Ridge Junction (Gunn-Barclay Divide, above waterfall gully)
waypoints.directions: From the spur road near the trailhead, take the faint climbers' path east into the forest rather than the maintained lake trail. Cross Barclay Creek on logs, leave the old roadbed and zigzag steeply up to a headwall at about 3,600 ft. The path veers east beneath cliff bands and drops briefly into the waterfall gully; climb steeply out the far side to where cairns lead onto moderate ground.

waypoints.name: Gunnshy Peak Summit
waypoints.directions: Keep heading east beneath a buttress, not north into slide alder and devil's club, and follow cairns through meadows along Tailgunner's south ridge to the saddle near 5,400 ft. Bypass Point 5,760 by dropping about 200 ft around its east side, climb to the saddle north of it, drop down the west slopes to about 5,200 ft to get around Gunn Peak's southwest buttress, make a rising traverse above Gunn Lake through talus and heather to the east ridge near 5,950 ft, then traverse west along and just south of the crest, scrambling to the summit.

waypoints.name: Alpental Ski Area / Snow Lake Trailhead parking lot
waypoints.note: Alpental Ski Area parking lot, the shared start for all Guye Peak routes. Stay off the private Strasse roads on the way to the talus below the west face.
waypoints.directions: From I-90 Exit 52 (West Summit) at Snoqualmie Pass, turn north onto Alpental Road, pass under the freeway, keep right at the fork just beyond the Pacific Crest Trail access, and drive about 1.4 miles to the Alpental Ski Area lot, with the Snow Lake trailhead across the road. A Northwest Forest Pass is required. Do not drive or park on the private Strasse roads off the access road.

waypoints.name: Lunch Ledge belay (~300 ft on route)
Guye Peak summit (south summit, has the summit register; traverse endpoint)
Snow Lake / Alpental Trailhead
waypoints.note: Large gravel lot off Alpental Rd (I-90 exit 52); Northwest Forest Pass required, there is no established path to the West Face talus, and the private 'Strasse' roads through the Alpental development are closed to climbers.
waypoints.directions: Take I-90 to Exit 52 and follow Alpental Road to its end at the Alpental/Snow Lake trailhead, around 3,100 to 3,120 feet. Park in the large gravel lot; a Northwest Forest Pass is required. There is no established path to the West Face talus; stay off the private roads through the Alpental development, which have been closed to climbers since 2021.

waypoints.name: Talus cone & rocky streambed below West Face
waypoints.note: Boot path climbs through slide alder onto an open talus cone, then a rising traverse crosses a rocky streambed (often dry) to the base of the face — helmet strongly advised, climber-kicked rockfall is common here.
waypoints.directions: Make your way from the trailhead to the talus cone below the west face by a line that stays off the private 'Strasse' roads through the Alpental development; there is no established path. On the talus, make a rising traverse toward its north end, with helmets on against rockfall from your own party and anyone above.

waypoints.name: Large tree-covered ramp
waypoints.note: Exit the streambed right onto a broad, rising ramp with full-grown trees that traverses the whole west face north to south; some parties belay this, most scramble it.
waypoints.directions: Traverse up the talus to the rocky streambed at its north end (often dry), scramble up the streambed, where some parties belay the steepest part, and exit right onto the very large tree-covered ramp that rises across the face from north to south.

waypoints.name: Notch at top of the ramp
waypoints.note: Ramp ends at a notch; pass through it to climber's right into a wide gully where the crux pitch begins.
waypoints.directions: Follow the ramp south across the face; most parties scramble it, some belay. At its end, climb about 40 ft of solid rock to a second, grassy ramp and the notch.

waypoints.name: Crux crack/face pitch
waypoints.note: Low 5th-class crack/face for ~30 ft easing to Class 4 through alpine trees for about half a rope length; belay just below the notch above.
waypoints.directions: Pass through the notch to climber's right into a wide gully, where the crux pitch begins.

waypoints.name: Guye Peak summit
waypoints.note: South summit (5,168 ft), where the route tops out; the north summit is a few feet higher. Small register, open views over Snoqualmie Pass and across to Cave Ridge and Snoqualmie Mountain.
waypoints.directions: Climb the steep crack and face for about 30 ft, then Class 4 through rock and alpine trees for about half a rope length to the top.

waypoints.name: Guye Peak–Cave Ridge saddle
waypoints.note: Standard walk-off descent drops from the north/true summit down to this saddle before continuing north to rejoin the Snow Lake/Cave Ridge trail system back to Alpental.
waypoints.directions: Follow the climber's path around the east side of the middle summit to the notch between the south and middle summits and rappel the loose, mossy slab into the gully (not from the tree at its top). Descend the gully and slabs east around the north summit, scramble an easy gully to the notch on its north side, and follow the scrambler's trail down to the saddle.

waypoints.name: Alpental / Snow Lake Trailhead
waypoints.note: Cave Ridge/Snoqualmie Mountain boot path leaves about 100 ft south of the signed Snow Lake Trail sign.
waypoints.directions: Take I-90 to Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West), turn left (north) under the freeway onto Alpental Road and follow it about 1.3 miles to its end at the Alpental ski area parking and the Snow Lake trailhead, around 3,100 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and a free self-issue Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit is available at the trailhead.

waypoints.name: Cave Ridge – Guye Peak saddle
waypoints.note: Reached via the Cave Ridge Trail (~1.5 mi); turn right (south) along the ridge toward Guye's north summit.
waypoints.directions: Take the climbers' path that leaves the pavement about 100 ft south of the Snow Lake Trail sign, the one that serves Snoqualmie Mountain and Cave Ridge rather than the West Face talus. It climbs steeply through forest past a clearing near 4,000 to 4,200 ft to the saddle between Cave Ridge and Guye Peak, about 1.5 miles in.

waypoints.name: Guye Peak north summit
waypoints.note: Standard North Route tops out here; the 'Hidden Ridge' variation adds a short rappel/toprope pitch nearby.
waypoints.directions: From the saddle, scramble the steep gully and ridge up to Guye's north summit, class 3 when snow-free and considerably more serious under snow. Around 4,840 ft the gully runs into a large rock face: take the left-hand option (a steep snow traverse in season), not the right, which leads into an awkward moat.

waypoints.name: PCT North / Snoqualmie Pass North Trailhead
waypoints.directions: Take I-90 to Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West) and turn left under the freeway onto Alpental Road. In about 0.1 mile take the first right, signed for the parking pass, and in another 0.1 mile keep right for the main Pacific Crest Trail North lot. A Northwest Forest Pass is required.

waypoints.name: Guye Peak summit
waypoints.directions: Follow the old Commonwealth Basin trail about 1.4 miles until Guye's summit bears roughly west-northwest (290 degrees), then leave the trail and go straight uphill. The slope starts at about 45 degrees, turns northwest into the gully proper for about 40 m, and steepens steadily to roughly 70 degrees near the top. The gully exits onto the ridge between the summits, not on one; follow the crest from there to the top.

waypoints.name: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road
Eldorado Creek trailhead (Cascade River Road mile 20)
waypoints.note: Gravel pullout on Cascade River Road (~mile 20 from Marblemount, about 3 miles short of the road's end); privy at trailhead, wilderness permit (from the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center) required for overnight camping in North Cascades NP.
waypoints.directions: Drive Cascade River Road from Marblemount about 20 miles to the large gravel pullout that serves as the Eldorado trailhead, at roughly 2,100 feet. The final stretch of road is gravel, and there's a privy at the trailhead. A wilderness permit, picked up in person at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center, is required for overnight camping in North Cascades National Park. Best conditions on this route typically run mid-July through early September, once the road is open and the Cascade snowpack has consolidated.

waypoints.name: Talus/boulder field entry
waypoints.note: After ~1,500 ft of forest gain the trail gives way to a cairned talus slope with cliffs on the left; stay off the climbers' path in fog, it's easy to lose in the boulders.
waypoints.directions: Find the current log crossing of the Cascade River (it shifts from year to year, so scout up- and downstream if it is gone), then follow the unmaintained climbers' path as it switchbacks steeply through timber and brush for about 1,500 ft to the start of the cairned talus field, with cliffs on the left.

waypoints.name: Roush Creek Basin camps
waypoints.note: Small, level camp spots on the ridge at 6,100-6,400 ft in the basin below Eldorado Glacier; last reliable tent sites before roped glacier travel.
waypoints.directions: Cross the boulders staying climber's right, since cairn lines trending left lead into cliffier ground. Follow the climbers' trail up a rib to a basin at 5,500-5,800 ft, drop slightly into the Roush Creek drainage for the last reliable running water, then climb again to the camps at 6,100-6,400 ft at the toe of the Eldorado Glacier.

waypoints.name: Eldorado Glacier gain point
waypoints.note: Rope up here; snowfields lead onto the Eldorado Glacier just west (left) of the rocky ridge above Roush Creek Basin.
waypoints.directions: Rope up at camp and climb the snowfields above onto the Eldorado Glacier, keeping just west (left) of the rocky ridge above the basin.

waypoints.name: Eldorado ice-cap / Inspiration Glacier high camp
waypoints.note: Common high camp on the Eldorado-Inspiration ice cap near the base of Eldorado's east ridge, used as the base for the traverse across the Inspiration Glacier to Klawatti Col.
waypoints.directions: Climb the crevassed Eldorado Glacier north to the broad Eldorado-Inspiration ice cap and the high camp near the base of Eldorado's east ridge.

waypoints.name: Klawatti Col
waypoints.note: Broad saddle on Klawatti Peak's south side with sheltered bivy sites on rock benches beside the glacier; both the Southeast Face and the SW Buttress start from here.
waypoints.directions: Roped, make the long, mostly flat traverse east and north across the Inspiration Glacier to the col. The ice cap is featureless and whiteouts are common, so carry a bearing or a track and be ready to navigate blind.

waypoints.name: Glacier crossing below the face
waypoints.note: Stay roped crossing the crevassed glacier toward the base of the face; open crevasses require route-finding, especially late season.
waypoints.directions: From the col, stay roped and head for the foot of the south-facing face, weaving around open crevasses.

waypoints.name: Bergschrund below the southeast face
waypoints.note: A short Class 4-5 rock pitch is needed to clear the bergschrund guarding the face; a rap sling has been reported on the right (east) side for the descent moat.
waypoints.directions: Climb directly up the snow flank until it pulls back from the rock at the bergschrund, which becomes a moat later in the season.

waypoints.name: Klawatti Peak
waypoints.note: True summit, a rock nunatak ringed by the Klawatti, McAllister, and Inspiration Glaciers; above the schrund, a short low-5th-class rock step gives way to several hundred feet of 40-55° snow.
waypoints.directions: Clear the bergschrund on a short class 4 to low-fifth rock step, or a snow bridge if one holds, then climb several hundred feet of 40-55 degree snow to the top of the face. From there the elongated summit crest is an easy scramble; its true high point is hard to pick out.

removed.wp: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road

waypoints.name: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road
Eldorado Creek trailhead (Cascade River Road mile 20)
waypoints.directions: From Seattle, take I-5 north then follow WA-20, the North Cascades Highway, east through Sedro-Woolley, Concrete and Rockport to Marblemount, then follow Cascade River Road south for about 20 miles to the Eldorado parking area near mile 20 — paved for the first 10 miles, gravel and washboard the rest of the way. Any overnight stay in the Eldorado/Klawatti zone requires a North Cascades National Park backcountry permit, available in advance on Recreation.gov or as a limited walk-up allocation from the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center or ranger station.

waypoints.name: Eldorado (East Ridge) camp
waypoints.directions: Cross the Cascade River near the trailhead on whatever log or ford is in that year, then climb the steep, unmaintained climbers' path through old growth to the boulder field and on into the Eldorado Creek and Roush Creek basin. Rope up there and climb the Eldorado Glacier to camp on the ice cap near the base of Eldorado's east ridge.

waypoints.name: Klawatti camp / col
waypoints.note: Camp south of Klawatti near the col dividing the Klawatti and McAllister Glaciers; SW Buttress start is minutes away.
waypoints.directions: Roped, traverse the Inspiration Glacier north-northeast past Eldorado's summit to Klawatti Col, the saddle between the Klawatti and McAllister glaciers on the peak's south side. The ice cap is flat and featureless and whiteouts are common, so carry a bearing or track.

waypoints.name: Klawatti Peak
waypoints.directions: The buttress stands minutes above the col camp. Cross the moat onto the rock, climb one to three short low-fifth pitches of loose rock up the buttress, then scramble along the elongated southwest crest to the summit, where the high point is not obvious.

removed.wp: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road

waypoints.name: Blue Lake TH
waypoints.directions: Drive SR 20 to the Blue Lake Trailhead on the south side of the highway, about 1 mile west of Washington Pass, at roughly 5,200 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park. The highway over the pass closes in winter.

waypoints.name: Chockstone Route start (shared)
waypoints.note: Shares its start with the Chockstone Route before breaking left onto steeper 5.11a terrain.
waypoints.directions: Hike the Blue Lake Trail and take the climbers' path into the basin below the Liberty Bell Group. Continue past South Early Winters Spire to the west side of the two Early Winters Spires and the base of the big chasm between them, where the Chockstone Route starts.

waypoints.name: Mowich Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: Mowich Lake has had no public road access since the SR 165 Fairfax Bridge south of Carbonado closed permanently in April 2025; the lake is reached only on foot via the Wonderland Trail from another part of the park, with a wilderness permit. The road in ran from Buckley on SR 165 through Wilkeson and Carbonado, then up the gravel Mowich Lake Road to its end at the lake.

waypoints.name: Liberty Cap
waypoints.directions: Take the trail 3 to 4 miles up into Spray Park and leave it near 6,400 ft on a beaten path toward the snow. Cross the Flett Glacier between Echo and Observation Rocks, climb to the saddle just east of Observation Rock, then follow the Ptarmigan Ridge crest south to high camp near 10,300 ft. From camp drop west onto the Mowich Glacier, cross the bergschrund near 9,800 ft, and climb the face through the rock band to the Liberty Cap Glacier and Liberty Cap.

waypoints.name: Columbia Crest
waypoints.directions: Cross the broad, gentle saddle southeast of Liberty Cap and climb the low-angle summit dome to the crater rim.

waypoints.name: Camp Schurman (Emmons-Winthrop descent)
waypoints.directions: Descend the Emmons-Winthrop route northeast off the summit dome, keeping to the Emmons track rather than the busier Disappointment Cleaver track on the south side, and follow it down the glacier corridor to Camp Schurman beside Steamboat Prow at about 9,400 ft.

waypoints.name: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road
Eldorado Creek / Cascade River Road TH
waypoints.directions: From Seattle, take I-5 north then follow WA-20, the North Cascades Highway, east through Sedro-Woolley, Concrete and Rockport to Marblemount, then follow Cascade River Road south for about 20 miles to the Eldorado parking area near mile 20 — paved for the first 10 miles, gravel and washboard the rest of the way. Any overnight stay requires a free North Cascades National Park backcountry permit; reserve in advance on Recreation.gov or pick up a limited walk-up permit in person at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center.

waypoints.name: Eldorado (East Ridge) camp
waypoints.directions: Walk back a short way along the road to the current crossing of the Cascade River, a log or a braided ford that shifts year to year, then climb the steep unmaintained climbers' path through old growth to a boulder field, cross Eldorado Creek and continue into the Eldorado Creek basin meadows. Rope up and climb the Eldorado Glacier to the camp near 7,600 ft where the Eldorado and Inspiration ice meet.

waypoints.name: Base of Tepeh Towers
waypoints.note: ~45 min glacier walk N/NW from camp to where the towers rise off the Eldorado ice cap.
waypoints.directions: Rope up and walk the glacier north-northwest for about 45 minutes to where the towers rise out of the icecap, on the arete that divides the Inspiration Glacier from the McAllister Glacier.

waypoints.name: Tepeh Towers
waypoints.note: One short low-5th-class pitch above the moat, then a scramble to the top.
waypoints.directions: Climb high on the glacier to where it rests against the rock and cross the moat. One short low-fifth-class pitch, then easy scrambling, leads to the summit.

removed.wp: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road

waypoints.name: Blue Lake Trailhead
waypoints.note: Blue Lake Trail #314 trailhead on SR-20; shared approach for Liberty Bell and South Early Winters Spire (NW Forest Pass required).
waypoints.directions: Drive SR-20 to the signed Blue Lake Trailhead on the south side of the highway about a mile west of Washington Pass, between mileposts 161 and 162, roughly 42 miles east of Newhalem. The paved lot requires a Northwest Forest Pass or day fee. The highway is closed in winter.

waypoints.name: South Early Winters Spire
waypoints.note: True summit of South Early Winters Spire, between Liberty Bell and Blue Lake Peak.
waypoints.directions: Follow the Blue Lake Trail about 1 to 1.25 miles to the clearing on its northwest side, then take the climbers' path up talus into the basin below the west face. The route starts on a bolted face about 20 ft downhill of the large chockstone-filled chimney, just left of the Northwest Face's first pitch, and its top pitches finish up the Southwest Rib to the summit.

waypoints.name: Hurricane Ridge Visitor Center (High Ridge Trailhead)
waypoints.note: Start at the east end of the Hurricane Ridge parking lot on the paved Cirque Rim path onto High Ridge Trail; restrooms/potable water here in summer, none beyond this point.
waypoints.directions: Drive Hurricane Ridge Road about 17 miles south from Port Angeles — Race Street off Highway 101 — to the road's end at the Hurricane Ridge Visitor Center, around 5,250 ft. Park in the visitor center lot and start at its east end, on the paved Cirque Rim path onto the High Ridge Trail. Come early, since parking here fills. The seasonal contact station has restrooms and potable water, and it is the last of either — there is no reliable water anywhere past the lot.

waypoints.name: Sunrise Point spur junction
waypoints.note: Optional 0.2-mi dead-end spur to a panoramic overlook; stay on the main High Ridge/Sunrise Ridge Nature Trail toward Klahhane Ridge to continue.
waypoints.directions: From the east end of the visitor center lot, follow the paved High Ridge Trail uphill to the junction with the short spur to Sunrise Point; stay on the main trail toward Klahhane Ridge.

waypoints.name: Morse Creek valley overlook spur
waypoints.note: Short spur trail to a viewpoint over the Morse Creek/Elwha drainages.

waypoints.name: Mount Angeles trail fork (Klahhane Ridge split)
waypoints.note: Bear left to stay on the climbers' path toward the Mount Angeles summit block; the right fork continues along Klahhane Ridge toward Victor Pass/Lake Angeles and is not the summit route.

waypoints.name: Exposed Class 3 crux step below summit block
waypoints.note: ~40-ft exposed move on loose, rotten rock near the top of the scree bowl where the boot path fades into talus; a fall here could exceed 100 ft, many parties spot or rope this step.

waypoints.name: Mount Angeles summit
waypoints.note: True summit (6,454 ft), high point of the Klahhane Ridge/Hurricane Ridge area with views over the Elwha Valley, Port Angeles, and the Strait of Juan de Fuca.

waypoints.name: Dingford Creek Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From I-90 Exit 34, turn north on 468th Ave SE and in about 0.6 mile turn right onto the Middle Fork Road (FR 56). Follow it about 12 miles to the Taylor River junction, stay right on the Middle Fork Road, and continue roughly 6 miles on rougher road to the Dingford Creek Trailhead at about 1,400 ft, with parking on the right. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and higher clearance helps on the last stretch.

waypoints.name: Mount Price Summit
waypoints.directions: Climb Dingford Creek Trail 1005 past Pumpkinseed Falls and several stream crossings to the fork at about 3 miles, bear right on the Hester Lake Trail, and gain about 1,000 ft in 2.5 miles to Hester Lake. Continue to Little Hester Lake and climb the boulder field directly south of it to Price's east ridge, east of the 5,440-ft subpeak. Traverse the steep north side of the ridge to the 5,400-ft col just east of the summit, then scramble the final ridge to the top.

waypoints.name: Klipchuck Campground, with Early Winters nearby
Cutthroat Creek Trailhead
waypoints.note: Turn off Hwy 20 ~4.4-4.5mi east of Washington Pass onto FR-400 (signed for Cutthroat Lake/Creek Trail), drive ~1mi to trailhead lot (restrooms). From the trailhead, leave trail and bushwhack/hike up through open forest (no maintained trail) toward the wall, gaining elevation and traversing left; ~1-1.5hr to the base.
waypoints.directions: Turn off Hwy 20 about 4.4 to 4.5 miles east of Washington Pass onto Forest Road 400, signed for the Cutthroat Lake/Creek Trail, and drive roughly a mile to the trailhead lot. The lot sits at about 4,500 ft and has restrooms. Don't confuse this with the Cutthroat Peak approach, which starts from an unmarked highway pullout about 1.5 miles west of Washington Pass with no maintained trail.

waypoints.name: Base of Cutthroat Creek Wall (right-hand shoulder)
waypoints.note: No established trail; hike through woods then traverse rocky benches to the wall base, ~1-1.5 hrs. Narcos is a 5.9 trad, PG13 line.
waypoints.directions: From the lot, walk up through the woods toward the wall on an unmaintained, intermittently cairned climbers' line, gaining elevation quickly, then traverse left through open forest and across slabby benches to a shoulder at the base of the wall's right-hand side. Allow an hour to an hour and a half.

waypoints.name: Little Liberty Bell / Cutthroat Creek Wall (formation high point)
waypoints.directions: From the shoulder, climb the low-angle, left-trending ramp of cracks and follow Narcos's five pitches; the fourth pitch joins the Wright-Pond corner and the fifth finishes on Wright-Pond's final blocky pitch to the top. Descend by rappelling the Wright-Pond line, four double-rope rappels with 60 m ropes, to the base.

removed.wp: Klipchuck Campground, with Early Winters nearby

waypoints.name: Blue Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From Winthrop, drive SR-20 west about 30 miles, over Washington Pass, to the signed Blue Lake Trailhead on the south side of the highway about a mile west of the pass, at roughly 5,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass, Interagency pass or day-use fee is required to park. SR-20 is gated over Washington Pass through the winter, so there is no drive-up access until it reopens in spring.

waypoints.name: North Early Winters Spire
waypoints.directions: Follow the Blue Lake Trail about 1.5 miles to the signed climbing-access junction just past a small stream (the last water), then take the climbers' path up slabs, talus and heather into the basin under the west faces and traverse north along the base to a corner and crack leading to a treed ledge. Five pitches of 5.8-5.9 corners, wide cracks and an offwidth finish left around a roof to the summit.

waypoints.name: Klipchuck Campground, with Early Winters nearby
Cutthroat Peak Climbers Trail Pullout (Hwy 20, ~1.5 mi W of Washington Pass)
waypoints.note: Roadside pullout on north side of SR-20; climbers trail leaves east end, crosses State Creek to basin below Cutthroat Peak.
waypoints.directions: Park in the long pullout on the north side of Highway 20 about 1.5 miles west of Washington Pass, at roughly 5,200 feet. The climbers' trail leaves the east end of the pullout and crosses State Creek into the basin below Cutthroat Peak — the same start used for the South Buttress route, so once you're up in the boulder field bear right and north toward the North Ridge Notch rather than left toward the South Buttress gully.

waypoints.name: North Ridge Notch
waypoints.directions: Follow the climbers' trail from the east end of the pullout across State Creek, up the brushy path into the meadow and on into the boulder field. There, bear right and north into the basin beneath the North Ridge Notch instead of left toward the South Buttress gully. One loose, runout 5.7 pitch with marginal small-cam protection gains the notch.

waypoints.name: Cutthroat Peak Summit
waypoints.directions: From the notch, climb a trough and an unprotected 5.6 slab traverse to the crest, then follow ramps and corners on the east (left) side of the crest. Downclimb a short 5.0 step off the last gendarme, cross the flat section of the ridge, and climb the 5.4 summit headwall to the top.

removed.wp: Klipchuck Campground, with Early Winters nearby

waypoints.name: Blue Lake Trailhead
waypoints.note: Blue Lake Trail #314 trailhead on SR-20; shared approach for Liberty Bell and South Early Winters Spire (NW Forest Pass required).
waypoints.directions: The Blue Lake Trailhead is on the south side of SR 20 (North Cascades Highway) a little under a mile west of Washington Pass, between mileposts 161 and 162, about 42 miles east of Newhalem or 31 miles west of Winthrop. The paved lot is small and fills early. A Northwest Forest Pass or day-use fee is required.

waypoints.name: South Early Winters Spire
waypoints.note: True summit of South Early Winters Spire, between Liberty Bell and Blue Lake Peak.
waypoints.directions: Follow the Blue Lake Trail about 1 to 1.25 miles to the clearing on the spire's northwest side, then take the climbers' path up talus and heather into the basin below the northwest face. Find the chockstone-filled chimney between the two formations; the route starts at the steep corner entered by a traverse, just right of the bolted Mojo Rising start. Climb six pitches to the summit.

waypoints.name: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road
Eldorado Creek Trailhead (Cascade River Road)
waypoints.note: Standard Eldorado Peak approach start; cross the Cascade River on a log downstream of the parking area.
waypoints.directions: Drive Cascade River Road about 20 miles from Marblemount to the large Eldorado Creek trailhead parking area at road mile 20, around 2,100 ft. From the lot, backtrack a short distance downstream to find a log or ford crossing of the Cascade River and pick up the climbers' path heading east and upstream on the far bank. This is the shared Eldorado Peak approach, the same start the other Dorado Needle routes use.

waypoints.name: Eldorado Creek Basin camp
waypoints.note: Open-basin camp after the first two talus fields, en route to the higher glacier camps.
waypoints.directions: Follow the climbers' path up the west side of Eldorado Creek through forest and talus, staying right of the large windfall area and not crossing the creek. Cairns and flagging lead up and right into a broad open basin around 5,500 to 5,800 ft with scattered camps.

waypoints.name: Eldorado/Inspiration Glacier high camp
waypoints.note: High camp on the Inspiration Glacier shelf used for all Eldorado-area and Dorado Needle objectives.
waypoints.directions: Continue north over more talus and snow onto the Eldorado Glacier and up to the high camp on the Inspiration Glacier shelf near 7,400 to 7,600 ft, about 5.3 miles and 5,300 ft from the car.

waypoints.name: Inspiration–McAllister Glacier col
waypoints.note: Cross north from the Inspiration Glacier through this notch in the Tepeh Towers, about 8,000 ft, onto the McAllister Glacier.
waypoints.directions: Rope up and cross the Inspiration Glacier to the notch in the Tepeh Towers.

waypoints.name: McAllister Glacier below the gendarmes
waypoints.note: Ascend the McAllister Glacier to just below Dorado Needle's line of gendarmes; this is the start of the NW Ridge, the easiest (1940 first-ascent) line at 5.4.
waypoints.directions: Drop onto the McAllister Glacier, favouring its left (south) side to avoid a large crevasse that opens on the right later in the season. Climb the steep upper apron, about 30 degrees, northwest to its top below the line of gendarmes, and look for a safe moat crossing.

waypoints.name: Dorado Needle summit
waypoints.note: Three pitches of class 5.4 rock past the gendarmes gain the true summit.
waypoints.directions: Cross the moat and climb a short low-fifth-class pitch to the ridge crest, then short pitches of easy fifth-class rock past the gendarmes to the summit.

removed.wp: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road

waypoints.name: SR-20 Wine Spires pullout / Burgundy Col climbers' trail
waypoints.directions: Park at the roadside pullout on SR-20, about seven-tenths of a mile past the Cutthroat Lake Road turnoff and directly across the highway from the Wine Spires. The boot and climbers' trail for Burgundy Col begins right at this pullout, dropping off the road shoulder.

waypoints.name: Burgundy Creek bench camp — west side
Burgundy Col
waypoints.note: 7,770-ft notch separating the Wine Spires from Vasiliki Ridge, reached via steep talus/scree above the Bench camp.
waypoints.directions: From the pullout a boot/climbers' trail drops off the shoulder, crosses Early Winters Creek on logs or a rock-hop (a wet ford in early-season snowmelt), and climbs a timbered rib on the climber's-left side of the Burgundy Creek drainage, gaining about 2,000 ft over the first 1.5-2 miles to a broad flat bench at 6,400-6,600 ft. The bench is the last reliable water and can run dry by late summer; above it the trail continues up steep talus and scree to the col.

waypoints.name: Pernod Spire Summit
waypoints.directions: From Burgundy Col, cross to the east side and traverse south below the east walls, then climb obliquely up to the notch between Pernod and Chianti; from the notch the line goes up the northeast corner to the small summit block, which carries old first-ascent bolts worth backing up.

waypoints.name: Mount Washington Trailhead (FR 2419)
waypoints.directions: From US 101 in Hoodsport, take SR-119 (North Lake Cushman Road) about 9.4 miles to the T intersection, turn right on Forest Road 24, and in about 1.5 miles turn left on Forest Road 2419. Follow it up the Big Creek drainage about 6.6 miles, past the Mount Ellinor trailheads, to the road end at roughly 3,000 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

waypoints.name: Mount Washington - Summit
waypoints.note: SE Ridge / Shield Wall route, a 5.7 rock climb of about 13 pitches.
waypoints.directions: Walk the old roadbed past the standard route's trail entrance about 1,000 ft to just beyond the Big Creek crossing, then take the climbers' trail up a rock rib. At the base of the ridge's big rock section (about 3,700 ft) bear right around the rocks, follow the ridgeline until gendarmes force you right, then climb a gully up and left to the notch at the wall's left corner (about 4,850 ft). Climb the Shield Wall and the ridge above to the summit.

waypoints.name: Blue Lake Trailhead
waypoints.note: Blue Lake Trail #314 trailhead on SR-20; can also be approached via the hairpin curve east of Washington Pass.
waypoints.directions: Drive SR-20, the North Cascades Highway (closed over Washington Pass in winter), to the signed Blue Lake Trailhead near milepost 161, just west of Washington Pass: about 42 miles east of Newhalem, or about 30 miles west of Winthrop. Park in the lot at about 5,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or day pass is required.

waypoints.name: South Early Winters Spire
waypoints.note: South Arete tops out on the true summit of South Early Winters Spire.
waypoints.directions: Follow Blue Lake Trail #314 about 1.3 to 1.5 miles to a minor stream draining the basin below the Early Winters Spires, well short of Blue Lake, and leave the trail on the cairned climbers' path. Follow it up slabs, heather and talus beside the stream to the southwest toe of South Early Winters Spire, then climb the South Arete, a short slab crux, a chimney and the broken crest, to the summit.

waypoints.name: Hairpin Turn Pullout (Hwy 20)
waypoints.note: Dirt pullout at the hairpin switchback ~0.5-1mi east of Washington Pass, directly beneath the east faces of North/South Early Winters Spire; hike up Spire Gully to the NEWS-SEWS notch, then traverse left to the route base. Parties often descend via South Arete/Blue Lake Trail and hitchhike back to a car left here.
waypoints.directions: Drive SR-20 to Washington Pass (the highway is closed over the pass in winter), then continue east, downhill, to the big hairpin switchback just below the pass; from the Mazama side it is the hairpin you reach as the road climbs to the pass. Park in the dirt pullout at the hairpin, about 5,100 ft, directly below the east faces of the Early Winters Spires. This is not the Blue Lake Trailhead.

waypoints.name: South Early Winters Spire
waypoints.directions: Hike up Spire Gully, following occasional cairns, to the last large tree in the middle of the gully, then traverse right across talus (snow early in the season) to below the gully that leads to the notch between North and South Early Winters Spires. Traverse left to the foot of the east buttress and climb its nine pitches to the summit.

waypoints.name: Blue Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: Drive SR-20, the North Cascades Highway (closed over Washington Pass in winter), to the signed Blue Lake Trailhead near milepost 161, just west of Washington Pass: about 42 miles east of Newhalem, or about 30 miles west of Winthrop. Park in the lot at about 5,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or day pass is required.

waypoints.name: South Early Winter Spire Summit
waypoints.directions: Follow Blue Lake Trail #314 to the climbers' path and take it up to the base of the South Arete. From there head down and right along the base of the wall for about 10 minutes, losing some height to skirt steeper ground, to double cracks beside a fir tree; the four-bolt dihedral 100 ft farther on is the neighboring route. Climb the seven pitches to the South Arete and follow it to the summit.

waypoints.name: Blue Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: Drive SR-20, the North Cascades Highway (closed over Washington Pass in winter), to the signed Blue Lake Trailhead near milepost 161, just west of Washington Pass: about 42 miles east of Newhalem, or about 30 miles west of Winthrop. Early in the season the lot may still hold snow. A Northwest Forest Pass or day pass is required.

waypoints.name: South Early Winters Spire summit
waypoints.directions: Follow Blue Lake Trail #314 about 1.5 miles to the climbers' path and take it up into the basin west of the Liberty Bell group. Enter the couloir about 100 ft below the start of the South Arete, on its left, climb the wide lower gully, take the right branch at the fork through the narrowing, and from the small saddle at its top make one low fifth-class move and scramble to the summit.

waypoints.name: SR-20 Wine Spires pullout (milepost 166)
waypoints.note: Unsigned roadside pullout on SR-20, about 0.7 mile past the Cutthroat Lake Road turnoff; parking for all the Wine Spires.
waypoints.directions: Drive SR-20 to the unsigned roadside pullout near milepost 166, about 4 miles east of Washington Pass and 0.7 mile past the Cutthroat Lake Road turnoff. There is no sign, so watch your mileposts. SR-20 over the pass is closed in winter.

waypoints.name: Early Winters Creek crossing
waypoints.note: Drop about 200 ft from the pullout on a boulder-field path to ford or log-cross Early Winters Creek; last reliable, easy water before the climb steepens.
waypoints.directions: From the pullout, follow the climbers' path down through boulders and talus, losing about 200 ft, to Early Winters Creek, and cross it on logs.

waypoints.name: The Bench (6,500 ft camp)
waypoints.note: Broad, flat bench roughly halfway up the approach with several established tent sites; last practical camp before the scree grind to Burgundy Col.
waypoints.directions: Past the creek, follow the climbers' path up the timbered rib on the north side of Burgundy Creek, climbing steeply about 2,300 ft to the broad bench camp at about 6,500 ft, the staging area for the Wine Spires.

waypoints.name: Burgundy Col
waypoints.note: Class 2 scree notch on Silver Star's north ridge 3,700 ft above the creek crossing; from here the route leaves the main Silver Star Glacier trail and works east toward the Wine Spires.
waypoints.directions: From the bench, continue up the climbers' path through scree gullies, snow early in the season, to Burgundy Col at about 7,770 ft.

waypoints.name: East-side scree gully traverse below the Wine Spires
waypoints.note: Loose, unconsolidated scree gullies traversing the east side of the ridge toward Pernod's south face; rockfall risk from parties above, stay bunched or spread out with care.
waypoints.directions: From Burgundy Col, do not drop straight toward Pernod's south side. Instead traverse and scramble around the east, Silver Star Creek, side of the ridge below Chianti on loose scree gullies and fourth-class ground; if the ground is still walkable, you have not started the traverse.

waypoints.name: Pernod Spire summit
waypoints.directions: Continue the traverse to the notch between Pernod and Chablis at the base of the South Face, carrying a rope for the last moves. Climb two pitches: good cracks through a right-facing corner toward the bunny-ear notch, then a thin-hands splitter that finishes with an aid move off a bolt to the summit (5.9 A0).

waypoints.name: Alpental / Snow Lake Trailhead parking
waypoints.note: Park at the Alpental ski area lot; approach toward Guye Peak's south side.
waypoints.directions: From I-90 Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West), turn north under the freeway onto Alpental Road and follow it about 1.3 miles to the road end at the Alpental ski area lot, the Snow Lake trailhead parking, at about 3,100 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required. The side roads named Strasse are private and closed to climbers, on foot as well as by car.
