waypoints.name: Guye Peak
waypoints.note: Ascend the obvious south-side gully past chockstones, moving onto the South Spur to the summit; climbable summer or winter.
waypoints.directions: From Alpental Road, work onto Guye Peak's south side on public ground and find the single obvious gully cleaving it. Scramble the gully until one or two chockstones force you briefly left onto the face, regain it, and follow the South Spur to the south summit. For the high point, traverse north over the middle summit, make the roughly 30 m rappel from slung trees into the gap, and scramble up to the north summit.

waypoints.name: Alpental / Snow Lake Trailhead parking
waypoints.note: Park at the Alpental ski area lot; hike the Sahale ski track toward Guye Peak, then traverse boulder fields/slide alder to the cliff base.
waypoints.directions: From I-90 Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West), turn north under the freeway onto Alpental Road and follow it about 1.3 miles to the road end at the Alpental ski area lot, the Snow Lake trailhead parking, at about 3,100 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required. The side roads named Strasse are private and closed to climbers, on foot as well as by car.

waypoints.name: Guye Peak
waypoints.note: Low-5th-class rib climbing to the summit; a relatively easy technical way up Guye.
waypoints.directions: Walk up the Sahale ski track toward Guye for about 3/4 to 1 mile; where it fades, climb the boulder field and slide alder to the base of the cliff. Traverse east along the base past Blood Sport to a taller talus fan, go up it to the rib, and climb about five pitches of low fifth-class rock, dirt and trees to the south summit. For the high point, traverse north over the middle summit, rappel into the gap, and scramble to the north summit.

waypoints.name: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road
Eldorado Creek / Cascade River Road TH
waypoints.directions: From Seattle, take I-5 north to WA-20 and follow the North Cascades Highway east through Sedro-Woolley, Concrete, and Rockport to Marblemount. Turn south onto Cascade River Road and drive about 20 miles to the Eldorado parking area near mile 20, at roughly 2,100 feet. The first 10 miles are paved; the rest is gravel and washboard. Any overnight stay needs a free North Cascades National Park backcountry permit, so either reserve one on Recreation.gov ahead of time or stop at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center on your way in for one of the limited walk-up spots.

waypoints.name: Eldorado Creek basin
waypoints.note: Upper basin, above the boulder fields. From here climb to the notch in the ridge between Eldorado Creek and Roush Creek, about 6,200 ft, and descend a short third-class gully into the Roush Creek basin at the foot of the Eldorado Glacier.
waypoints.directions: Walk back down the road a short way to cross the Cascade River, on a log or by fording; the crossing shifts from year to year. Follow the steep, unmaintained climbers' path up through old-growth forest east of Eldorado Creek to the boulder field near 4,000 ft, climb about 1,000 ft of boulders, and continue into the Eldorado Creek basin near 5,500 ft.

waypoints.name: Eldorado camp (Inspiration Glacier flat)
waypoints.note: Good camps on rocks near the broad flat of the Inspiration Glacier.
waypoints.directions: Climb to the notch in the ridge between Eldorado Creek and Roush Creek, about 6,200 ft, and descend a short third-class gully into the Roush Creek basin. Rope up and climb the Eldorado Glacier to the broad flat where it meets the Inspiration Glacier, near 7,600 ft, and camp on the rocks at its edge.

waypoints.name: Eldorado Peak
waypoints.note: Broad, snow-covered ridge to the spectacular knife-edge summit; the standard/easiest route.
waypoints.directions: From camp, traverse the steep, exposed snow on the glacier's flank (crampons mandatory) to the lowest point of the south ridge, the left-hand skyline from camp, below an obvious crack leading to a U-shaped notch. Climb the crack to the notch, cross to the far side and climb cracks back to the knife-edge crest, follow the crest two pitches to a short downclimb, then scramble the broad upper ridge to the summit.

removed.wp: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road

waypoints.name: Hairpin Turn Pullout (Hwy 20)
waypoints.note: The route shares its lower pitches with the Direct East Buttress, breaking left where that route goes up its bolt ladder, so it uses the same east-side hairpin/Spire Gully approach.
waypoints.directions: Drive SR 20 (North Cascades Highway) to about half a mile east of Washington Pass and park in the dirt pullout at the obvious hairpin turn, at about 5,100 ft, directly below the east faces of the Early Winters Spires. This is the east-side start, not the Blue Lake trailhead west of the pass.

waypoints.name: South Early Winters Spire
waypoints.directions: Hike up the cairned Spire Gully to the last large tree, traverse right across talus (snow early season) to the gully that leads to the notch between North and South Early Winters Spire, then traverse left to the base of the east buttress before reaching the notch. Climb the shared Direct East Buttress pitches, break out left about halfway up onto the south-facing headwall, and follow its crack pitches to the summit.

waypoints.name: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road
Eldorado Creek Trailhead (Cascade River Road)
waypoints.note: Same start as the East Ridge; cross the Cascade River on a log downstream of the parking area.
waypoints.directions: Drive Cascade River Road to the Eldorado Creek trailhead at about road mile 20, elevation roughly 2,100 ft, and park in the trailhead lot. The climb starts by leaving the parking area and backtracking a short way downstream to find a log or a ford across the Cascade River, then picking up the climbers' path on the west side of Eldorado Creek. This is the same start the East Ridge uses; the trailhead-to-glacier approach is identical for both.

waypoints.name: Eldorado Creek Basin camp
waypoints.note: Open-basin camp option after the first two talus fields and a waterfall crossing.
waypoints.directions: Follow the climbers' path up the west side of Eldorado Creek, climbing steeply through old-growth forest with no water to a talus field around 4,000 ft. Continue up the talus, re-cross Eldorado Creek near a cairn at about 5,100 ft, and carry on up to the open basin.

waypoints.name: Eldorado/Inspiration Glacier high camp
waypoints.note: Base camp on the flat glacier shelf used to stage the Inspiration/McAllister glacier traverse.
waypoints.directions: Switchback up past 6,000 ft and drop through a short class 3 gully into Roush Creek basin (6,100-6,400 ft, reliable water). From the basin climb 20-30 degree snow onto the toe of the Eldorado Glacier around 7,500 ft, rope up, and camp on rock or moraine near the glacier shoulder.

waypoints.name: Inspiration–McAllister Glacier col
waypoints.note: Cross north across Inspiration Glacier to this col, then drop northwest onto the McAllister Glacier.
waypoints.directions: From high camp, rope up and cross north over the Inspiration Glacier to the col at about 8,000 ft where it meets the McAllister Glacier.

waypoints.name: McAllister Glacier crossing
waypoints.note: Descend the McAllister Glacier toward its southwest gap; navigate visible crevasses, especially late-season.
waypoints.directions: From the col, drop northwest onto the McAllister Glacier and descend toward its southwest gap, threading the visible crevasses, which open up late in the season.

waypoints.name: Marble Creek–McAllister pass
waypoints.note: Lowest gap on the SW side of the glacier; cross to the small Marble Creek side glacier, generally on the pass's east side.
waypoints.directions: Continue across the McAllister to the Marble Creek-McAllister pass, the lowest gap on the southwest side of the glacier, and cross onto the small Marble Creek side glacier, generally on the pass's east side.

waypoints.name: Base of Southwest Buttress gully
waypoints.note: A snow-filled gully roughly 700 vertical feet below the pass leads to the start of the buttress climbing.
waypoints.directions: From the pass, descend about 700 ft on the Marble Creek side to the foot of the prominent gully, which often holds snow all year.

waypoints.name: Dorado Needle summit
waypoints.note: 9-pitch, Grade III, 5.7-5.8 buttress tops out on the true summit after a left-leaning corner on the upper ridge.
waypoints.directions: Climb the gully to the toe of the buttress, minding the moat at the base of the rock, then follow about nine pitches of 5.7-5.8 cracks, slabs and gendarme traverses to the knife-edge summit ridge.

removed.wp: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road

waypoints.name: Alpental / Snow Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From I-90 Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West), turn north under the freeway onto Alpental Road and follow it about 1.3 miles to the road end at the Alpental ski area lot, the Snow Lake trailhead, at about 3,100 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit is required.

waypoints.name: The Tooth summit
waypoints.directions: Follow the Snow Lake Trail about 1.5 miles, fork off toward Source Lake, cross the talus and start up the standard line toward Pineapple Pass. Before the pass, break off north of the gully to three low-angle open-book corners just past the South Face start, and climb about four pitches: corner to a slung tree, a left-facing slab, face left of three cracks under a small roof, then the upper South Face to the summit.

waypoints.name: Index-Galena Road / North Fork Skykomish River Access (FR-63, ~Mile 10)
waypoints.note: Park at the snowplow turnaround by the bridge about 1 mile east of Galena; this is the last reliable water, none is found once you leave the road.
waypoints.directions: Drive US 2 to Skykomish, then head north on the Beckler River Road (FR-65) for about 15 miles and turn left (west) onto FR-63. A high-clearance vehicle is worth having for the last few miles. Park at the turnaround by the river crossing near Galena at about 1,150 feet; the pullout is unmarked and easy to drive past. No permits are needed, and the river here is the last dependable water, since there is none once you leave the road.

waypoints.name: Old Logging Road / 2300-ft Saddle
waypoints.note: After a steep, brush-free first 600 ft through downed timber, cross an old overgrown logging road at this saddle on the lower north slopes.
waypoints.directions: Leave the road on the side away from the river and climb steeply, off-trail, through downed timber; the first 600 ft are steep but brush-free. After crossing an old logging road, traverse obliquely left to a saddle at about 2,300 ft, where you cross a second old overgrown logging road.

waypoints.name: Hogsback Ridge Top
waypoints.note: The well-defined hogsback you've been following since ~2700 ft terminates here; continue straight uphill toward the cliff bands above.
waypoints.directions: Continue uphill from the saddle; at about 2,700 ft the slope narrows into a well-defined, fairly brush-free hogsback. Follow its crest to where it ends at about 3,300 ft.

waypoints.name: Cliff Band Traverse
waypoints.note: Large cliff bands block the north end of the peak between roughly 4200-4400 ft; traverse southeast below them to reach the mountain's west/northwest side.
waypoints.directions: From the top of the hogsback, continue straight uphill as the slope steepens toward the large cliff bands that block the north end of the peak at roughly 4,200 to 4,400 ft.

waypoints.name: 5940-ft Saddle Northwest of Summit
waypoints.note: Gain this saddle via the traverse; a possible schrund/moat forms here depending on season and snow cover before you turn onto the final ridge.
waypoints.directions: Traverse southeast beneath the cliff bands onto the mountain's west and northwest side to about 5,400 ft below the summit spires, then turn uphill and climb the wide gully and slope to the saddle just northwest of the summit. Watch for a moat or schrund as you near the saddle, depending on the season.

waypoints.name: Class 5 Step
waypoints.note: The final ridge is mostly Class 3, but two short sections here are Class 4-5; many parties place a rope for this exposed step.
waypoints.directions: From the saddle, scramble southeast along the airy crest, mostly class 3, to a short exposed mantle step of about ten feet near 6,100 ft where many parties rope up. Stay on the crest; ground to the north and east steepens quickly into permanent snow and cliffs.

waypoints.name: Spire Mountain
waypoints.note: True summit at the top of the west/northwest ridge scramble, with views over the Monte Cristo peaks and North Fork Skykomish valley.
waypoints.directions: Above the step, continue a short way up the ridge to the summit.

waypoints.name: Blue Lake Trailhead (SR-20)
waypoints.note: Route is on the south/southeast face near Direct East Buttress; reached from this trailhead by the Blue Lake Trail and the climbers' path to the base of the South Arete.
waypoints.directions: Drive SR-20 to the Blue Lake Trailhead at milepost 161, on the south side of the highway about 1 mile west of Washington Pass. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and the highway over the pass is closed in winter, usually from about November to April.

waypoints.name: South Early Winters Spire
waypoints.directions: Take the Blue Lake Trail and the climbers' path to the base of the South Arete, about 1 hour, then traverse down and right along the base of the wall past the Passenger's fir-tree and double-crack start and roughly 100 ft farther to a small left-facing dihedral with four bolts. Climb nine pitches of sustained face and crack up the southeast face to the summit.

waypoints.name: Alpental / Snow Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From I-90 take Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West) and turn north under the freeway. Take the second right onto Alpental Road and drive about 1.3 miles to its end at the Alpental Ski Area lot, about 3,100 ft, where the Snow Lake Trail starts. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, plus a free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit.

waypoints.name: The Tooth summit
waypoints.directions: Hike the Snow Lake Trail about 1.6 miles to the Source Lake turnoff and go left. Cross the Source Lake basin near 4,000 ft, crest the lip into Great Scott Bowl at about 4,400 ft, and climb toward Pineapple Pass. Below the pass, traverse left (west) along the base, past the Southwest Face, to the bolt line on the west-facing wall. Climb six bolted pitches, then a short scramble to the true summit.

waypoints.name: Blue Lake TH
waypoints.directions: Drive SR-20 to the Blue Lake Trailhead, about 1 mile west of Washington Pass at roughly 5,400 ft, and park in the trailhead lot. This is the west-side start for the Liberty Bell Group; the Blue Lake Trail leaves from here and runs about a mile and a half to the climbers' path. Plan the trip for the June to September window.

waypoints.name: Base of West Face
waypoints.note: Low-angle cracks lead to a tree-topped chimney on the left side of the west face; shares the start with the NW Corner.
waypoints.directions: Hike the Blue Lake Trail about 1.5 miles and turn left onto the climbers' trail marked by wooden posts into the basin below the Liberty Bell Group. Walk past South Early Winters Spire and the chockstone-filled chasm that splits the two spires, then traverse left along the base of North Early Winters Spire to the shared start with the Northwest Corner.

waypoints.name: North Early Winters Spire
waypoints.directions: Climb the West Face from the shared start with the Northwest Corner: a dirty chimney to a sandy ledge, a steep right-facing corner, a lieback and undercling pitch, then the thin tips-crack crux, and finish on low-angle cracks with a friction-slab traverse right to the top.

waypoints.name: Alpental / Snow Lake Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From I-90 take Exit 52 (Snoqualmie Pass West) and turn north under the freeway. Take the second right onto Alpental Road and drive about 1.3 miles to its end at the Alpental Ski Area lot, about 3,100 ft, where the Snow Lake Trail starts. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, plus a free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit.

waypoints.name: The Tooth summit (traverse start point)
waypoints.directions: Hike the Snow Lake Trail about 1.6 miles to the Source Lake turnoff and go left. Cross the Source Lake basin near 4,000 ft and climb Great Scott Bowl south toward Pineapple Pass. Near 5,100 ft, bear right up a rocky gully, keeping left of a large horn, to the pass. From Pineapple Pass, rope up and climb the South Face (5.4) to the summit.

waypoints.name: Bryant Peak (rappel)
waypoints.note: One mandatory rappel, about 50 ft, short but steep. Build or check the anchor carefully; the rock along this crest is poorer than on the Tooth's faces.
waypoints.directions: From the Tooth's summit follow the crest northwest toward Chair Peak. Right after the Tooth there is a short stretch of walking through trees, then exposed fourth- and low-fifth-class ridge on loose, sub-par rock to Bryant Peak, where the traverse makes its one rappel.

waypoints.name: Chair Peak
waypoints.note: End of the traverse. Descend by downclimbing to the saddle and then the steep southwest-facing gully back to the basin.
waypoints.directions: Below the rappel, continue along the crest northwest, on or near the ridge, to Chair Peak's summit.

waypoints.name: SR-20 Burgundy Col Pullout
waypoints.note: Long unmarked pullout on the east shoulder of SR-20 near milepost 165-166, about 4 miles east of Washington Pass; the climber's trail drops down the embankment on the east side.
waypoints.directions: This route starts from a long, unmarked pullout on the east shoulder of State Route 20 near milepost 166, about 3.75 miles east of Washington Pass and directly across the valley from Silver Star Mountain, at roughly 4,310 feet. A climber's path drops down the embankment on the east side of the pullout into loose talus and forest, and you'll pass a registration box a few minutes down the trail.

waypoints.name: Early Winters Creek Crossing
waypoints.note: Trail descends ~200 ft from the pullout to ford/log-cross Early Winters Creek; last reliable, easy water before the steep climb begins.

waypoints.name: The Bench
waypoints.note: Flat forested camping bench with multiple established tent sites and views toward the Liberty Bell group; common first-night camp for a two-day trip.

waypoints.name: Burgundy Col
waypoints.note: 7,770-ft notch gained via 1,000+ ft of loose ball-bearing scree; routes on the north face are reached by scrambling/downclimbing loose rock or snow left from here.

waypoints.name: Twin-crack start
waypoints.note: ~5-10 min scramble down and around the north face from the col to a twin-crack system with obvious loose blocks about 60 ft up; roped climbing begins here.

waypoints.name: Burgundy Spire Summit
waypoints.note: P8 climbs left past an old bolt toward the top; parties who lose the line after P7 traverse ledges onto the North Face route's 5.10a squeeze chimney to finish, then downclimb/scramble or use the North Face rappel line to retreat.

waypoints.name: Mount Washington Trailhead (FR 2419)
waypoints.directions: The traverse has no trailhead of its own — it starts on Mount Washington's summit, so you drive to the Big Creek road-end off North Lake Cushman Road. Take FS Road 24 for about 1.5 miles, turn left onto FS Road 2419, and follow it roughly 6.6 miles up the Big Creek drainage to the small parking area at the road end, around 3,026 ft. Most parties finish on Mount Ellinor and walk out from its upper trailhead, which is a different parking area on the same road corridor, so leave a second car there or arrange a shuttle before you start.

waypoints.name: Mount Washington - Summit
waypoints.note: Climb Washington first, then traverse the ridge SW toward Ellinor.
waypoints.directions: Climb the steep boot path through forest to the meadow benches, then scree and talus on climber's left of the large loose gully to the southern ridgeline and across the exposed Dog Walk ledge. Take the goat trail up the right edge of the scree field below the false summit to the stone wind shelter, then a short Class 3-4 scramble to the summit.

waypoints.name: Mount Ellinor - Summit
waypoints.note: Traverse endpoint.
waypoints.directions: Follow the narrow crest southwest: first the Wedge, about 150 ft of low 5th on good holds, then sustained Class 4 past a series of gendarmes using hidden ledges below the obvious line, and a loose 50 ft downclimb. Where the crest gets too hard, drop into the basin and downclimb or bypass on a snow finger to rejoin Mount Ellinor's winter route to its summit.

waypoints.name: Mount Ellinor Upper Trailhead
waypoints.note: Standard descent/exit point via Mount Ellinor's upper trailhead.
waypoints.directions: Descend Mount Ellinor's standard trail through the subalpine slopes and forest to the upper trailhead at about 3,500 ft, where the shuttle car should be waiting.

waypoints.name: Alpental / Snow Lake Trailhead
waypoints.note: I-90 Exit 52, Alpental ski area parking lot; approach up valley past Source Lake toward Pineapple Pass basin for NE Face/Catscratch Couloir.
waypoints.directions: Take I-90 to Exit 52 and head north on Alpental Road to the Alpental Ski Area, where the trailhead starts from the parking lot at about 3,100 feet.

waypoints.name: Northeast Slabs base
waypoints.directions: Follow the Snow Lake Trail up the valley toward Source Lake. Once there is real snow cover, keep to the valley bottom rather than the summer switchbacks, which cross avalanche paths. Past Source Lake, traverse the talus below the cliff band toward the Tooth's northeast side, then climb the snow finger into the basin beneath the face and up the snow slope to the foot of the gully where the route starts; cache skis at the bottom of that slope. Roughly 2 to 2.5 miles and 1,500 to 2,000 ft from the car.

waypoints.name: The Tooth summit
waypoints.directions: Climb the gully and the slabs above it, five to six pitches of snow, ice and low fifth-class rock, to the North Ridge, then make the exposed move over the notch on the east face and follow easier ground to the summit.

waypoints.name: Cutthroat Creek Trailhead
waypoints.note: Same trailhead/approach as Narcos — both routes are on the same small wall, reached via the Cutthroat Creek Trail/FR-400 trailhead off Hwy 20.
waypoints.directions: From Winthrop, drive west on SR-20 for about 28 miles, to a point roughly 4.5 miles east of Washington Pass. Turn right onto Forest Service Road 400 and follow it one mile to the Cutthroat Creek Trailhead parking area, on the left side of the road.

waypoints.name: Klipchuck Campground, with Early Winters nearby
Base of the wall (shoulder at its right-hand side)
waypoints.note: No established trail; hike through woods then traverse rocky benches to the wall base, ~1-1.5 hrs. Wright-Pond is a 5.11a/b trad, PG13 line.
waypoints.directions: There is no trail. From the parking area, walk up through the woods toward the wall, gaining height quickly, then traverse left through open forest and across slabby benches to a shoulder at the base of the wall's right-hand side, about 1 to 1.5 hours from the car.

waypoints.name: Little Liberty Bell / Cutthroat Creek Wall (formation high point)
